g.text: okl — the Org Knowledge Layer
Decide up front how this codebase should be built. Have that put in front of the agent before every task — and re-graded the moment the code it governs moves.
1 · THE PLAN, UP FRONT
the seed: how you want this code built, decided before the work
THREE SOURCES FEED THE PLAN
the rules and specs the canon, ADRs and rules files you
you already wrote already keep, converted once into
typed records: okl seed <file>.json
this codebase /seed-from-codebase — an agent reads
the repo and proposes records, each
citing the file it found them in
outside material an article or guide, audited against
your canon before any of it lands
EVERY TYPE IS AN INSTRUCTION, NOT A PARAGRAPH
one shape, whatever the type — when you see X, do Y:
Rule a convention this codebase follows
Decision a trade-off already made, and the reason
Gate an armed check, and the defect it catches
Defect something that went wrong here once
Tombstone a name that was retired, so it stays dead
A paragraph cannot be routed into an action. These can.
THE VERDICT IS PART OF THE PLAN
an audit of one guide found all 10 of its stated items
already covered — while its own code examples broke
canon three times. Audit the examples, not the advice.
The verdict is kept, so nobody adopts it again later.
WHAT DOES NOT GO IN
generic advice ("write tests") crowds out the records
specific enough to act on. Anything you cannot cite is
a guess that will be injected into every future task.
SCOPE DECIDES HOW FAR IT TRAVELS
org → every connected repo, so a lesson paid for once
protects the next project. repo:<name> → stays here,
so a local quirk never fires in someone else's work.
2 · IN FRONT OF THE AGENT
every task, before the first line — not filed somewhere
THE TASK ARRIVES
"add an endpoint that returns an invoice"
SELECTED, NOT SKIMMED
scope filter → interest filter (tags) → BM25 rank
→ top-k cutoff, and it says how many it trimmed.
A 300-line rules file is read once and skimmed after;
this hands over only what matches, action first.
WHAT LANDS IN THE CONTEXT
FIX: ownership predicate missing
when you see: a fetch by id with no owner in WHERE
→ add the caller's id to the WHERE clause; 404 on
no match, so a probe cannot confirm the row exists
FAIL-CLOSED
unreachable, unconfigured and 401 all exit non-zero.
"No lesson applies" and "nobody was asked" look
identical to an agent, and only one of them is safe.
HOW IT REACHES THE AGENT
UserPromptSubmit hook — into context, before the turn
MCP okl_check · okl_record · okl_search
CLI for humans · CI: okl drift --gate on every PR
WHEN THE BUDGET IS SMALL
--format actions returns the imperative list alone:
roughly 250 tokens at limit=3, against ~4,400 for the
full briefing. A subagent on one focused subtask still
gets the rules without paying for the prose.
3 · RE-GRADED AS CODE MOVES
the part a document cannot do
A RECORD NAMES THE CODE IT GOVERNS
files: "src/api/**, src/auth/**"
the paths whose behaviour this record is about
DRIFT IS A QUESTION GIT CAN ANSWER
the last commit touching those paths, against the
timestamp of the record's last verification. Code
newer than the stamp means the rule may now be
describing something that has already changed.
A STAMP IS EVIDENCE, NEVER A CLAIM
okl verify <id> --run "pytest -q" --expect "passed"
runs the check, reads the real outcome, and requires
the positive signal — exit 0 cannot self-certify.
Command and result are stored on the record.
STALE FAILS THE PR THAT MADE IT STALE
okl drift --gate is a mechanical grader with no stake
in the claim. Not a warning in a file nobody opens.
TIME ATTACKS EVERY STAMP
TTL decays an un-re-earned stamp to STALE, and
okl metric scores recurrence-after-arming — the one
number the system cannot flatter itself on.
RE-EARN IT; DO NOT RE-STAMP IT
clearing drift by re-recording with --verified is the
one move the tool refuses. Run the check again — a
record's own tests are usually the right --run. A
stamp you can award yourself measures nothing.
THE STORE — typed, so a briefing can be routed rather than read
NODE TYPES
Defect · Rule · Gate · Decision
Tombstone · Retraction · Claim
PriorArt · Vocabulary · Entity
EDGES
CATCHES · REFUTES · RETRACTS
SUPERSEDES · VERIFIED_ON
RECURS_IN · ENCODES
TAGS
a closed vocabulary; a repo
declares its interests, so
off-subject records never rank
STORAGE
OKL_DATABASE_URL: one env var,
sqlite:///okl.db → postgresql://
BM25 (SQLite) / ts_rank (PG)
THE SHARED SERVICE
one instance many repos point at
OKL_TOKEN gates every route but
/health, which stays open to probe
"WHY NOT JUST WRITE A GOOD SPEC?"
Write the spec. This does not replace one — the rules and specs you already wrote
are the first thing it imports.
A spec states the intent for one piece of work. This carries the standing intent of
the codebase, and it is mostly not a ledger of bugs: the largest share by far is
conventions this code follows, then the trade-offs already decided and why, the
gates armed and what each catches, the outside advice vetted, the names retired.
What went wrong here is the smaller part of it. Then three things a document cannot do:
SELECTED a rules file is read once and skimmed forever after. Only the records
matching this task are handed over, action first, inside the budget.
ENFORCED the read runs in a hook and fails closed. A spec cannot block a task
that never opened it.
RE-GRADED a spec is exactly as true as the day it was written, and nothing tells
you when that stopped being true. A record names the files it governs,
git says when they last moved, and CI fails on the difference.
MEASURED — held-fixed A/B, blind judge≠generator
briefed 4–8% against a baseline of 33–50%
three runs, n=24 each, 0% harness failures
The baseline arm receives no briefing and never
changed, yet moved 17 points across those runs.
That is the noise floor: the gap survives it,
differences inside it are not interpretable.
